briefing.headline: OpenAI Orion and DeepSeek R2 escalate AGI compute arms race ahead of Q4 deadlines

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs race toward multimodal AGI thresholds while regulatory scrutiny intensifies. US-China compute restrictions tighten as new models demonstrate emergent capabilities. Investment surges past $11B this quarter amid safety concerns.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released Orion-2 with advanced reasoning benchmarks topping 92%. Anthropic's Claude 4 and Google's Gemini 3.5 compete closely while Meta open-sources Llama 4.5. DeepSeek R2 from China matches GPT-5 level performance. xAI Colossus cluster expands to 200k H100s.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. New EU AI Act enforcement targets agentic workflows. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for multi-agent and BCI applications.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC ramps 2nm production for AI chips while Microsoft and Google announce $50B combined data center builds. NVIDIA Blackwell supply constraints persist. Saudi Arabia joins sovereign AI compute race with 100k GPU cluster.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first AGI system emerge from a US lab or a distributed open-source coalition by 2028?
